current.description:
The index number of the page currently being viewed or returned in the paginated dataset.

It determines which "window" of records the user or client is requesting from the service. 'current' must be greater than or equal to 0. In typical usage, a value exceeding the total available number of pages (see 'pages' field) will result in either an empty result set or service-side auto-reset to the maximum page index, depending on the implementation. This field is required so that navigation state is never ambiguous in paged responses.

Example: If a dataset contains 200 records and 'limit' is 50, 'pages' will be 4. 'current' = 2 would mean records 101-150.

limit.description:
The maximum number of records to be displayed per page of results.

This allows clients or users to control the chunk size of paginated responses, which is crucial for performance and client-side rendering. 'limit' should be bounded by the server (e.g., typical values are 10, 25, 50, 100) to prevent excessively large page requests. Service implementations can enforce upper/lower bounds for this value. Always required for calculating offsets and results windows.

Example: Setting 'limit' to 25 means only 25 records will be shown per page.

records.description:
The total count of database records that match the query criteria, before pagination is applied.

This informs the client/application of the dataset's full cardinality so navigation controls, summaries, and progress indicators can be generated. 'records' must be non-negative and provides context for the entire pagination UI, even when only a subset of results are currently returned.

pages.description:
The calculated total number of pages based on 'records' and 'limit'.

'pages' is equal to 'records / limit' with ceiling, ensuring that the last page reflects any partial record sets. This is essential for accurate navigation and for validating the 'current' value. If 'records' is 0, 'pages' is still 0 (an empty result set). This field encodes boundary conditions for paging logic and user experience.

Example: For 120 records and limit 50, 'pages' will be 3.

is_active.description:

Deactivated accounts remain in the database but cannot log in or use admin features.

is_blocked.description:
True if the admin is suspended or blocked from accessing admin features.

Blocked status may be used for temporary suspensions or as the result of moderation investigations.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the admin account was created.

updated_at.description:

deleted_at.description:

IDiscussionBoardAdmin.IAuthorized.description:
Authorization response after admin join/login/refresh. Contains administrator identity and JWT token pair enabling further authenticated activity on the platform.

The payload provides a strong root of trust (id, JWT) for admin operations, supporting stateless moderation, session renewal, and compliance-valid traceability. Id is the canonical administrator UUID. Token is the session's JWT bundle, permitting secure privilege escalation, account management, and audit events. This DTO structure ensures identity, compliance, and traceability for all admin operations post-authentication.

Never contains credentials or password-related fields. Matches the requirements for audited moderator state transitions and platform security best practices.

IDiscussionBoardAdmin.ILogin.description:
Administrator login request data structure.

Used for authenticating administrators from the discussion_board_admins table. Request must include the administrator's unique email address and password (in plain text, never hashed). Upon successful authentication, secure session tokens are issued. IP, href, and referrer fields provide session tracking and audit information for compliance and traceability, as required for self-login flows. These fields are necessary for recording login attempts and session context, consistent with platform policy on administrative oversight.

Passwords are only accepted as plain text in this API; backend is responsible for hashing and secure comparison with the password_hash field in the database. This schema aligns with both security best practices and business requirements for admin authentication and session context recording.

email.description:
Administrator's unique email address used for login and notification.

Must match the email field of discussion_board_admins and be unique among all admins. Validated using strict RFC 5322 email format. Only existing, active admins may login.

password.description:
Administrator's plain-text password for authentication.

Must be securely transmitted to the backend and will never be returned or stored in responses. The backend hashes and compares this value against the password_hash in discussion_board_admins for authentication.

oneOf.description: Administrator's IP address (IPv4 or IPv6) for audit and session tracking; may be null or omitted if not available.
Administrator's IP address (IPv4 or IPv6) for audit and session tracking; may be null or omitted if not available.
Null value if IP is not provided by client.

ip.description:
Administrator's IP address for audit trail. Can be null or omitted if unavailable (server can infer if not provided).

Needed for session record in discussion_board_admin_sessions. Used to comply with audit/tracing requirements on admin logins.

href.description:
Current page URL from which admin login is requested (session context).

Required for admin self-login flows and session record in discussion_board_admin_sessions. Enables security auditing and user journey analysis.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL (previous page) when login is initiated (session context).

Required for audit trail and security analytics; must be provided in all admin login attempts for proper session context capture.

IDiscussionBoardAdmin.IRefresh.description:
Administrator JWT token refresh request structure.

Used for rotating JWT access and refresh tokens, maintaining secure stateless sessions for platform administrators. This schema is referenced on /auth/admin/refresh and must include the current valid refresh token provided at login or previous refresh. On success, new tokens and session data are returned in IDiscussionBoardAdmin.IAuthorized.

The field maps to business logic for administrator authentication and secure JWT rotation policies. Security checks require that the refresh token is strictly validated and managed according to core JWT/session policies and audit compliance.

refreshToken.description:
Current valid administrator refresh token. Used to authorize secure session renewal.

Must be a valid, unexpired, non-revoked JWT refresh token previously issued at admin login. Session and token data are cross-checked against discussion_board_admin_sessions and discussion_board_admins tables to ensure validity.

key.description:
Unique configuration key for searching a specific system-level setting.

This value must match the 'key' column (unique constraint, primary lookup field) defined in the discussion_board_system_settings Prisma table. Filtering is case-sensitive and supports both exact and partial match semantics for administrator queries.

The key enables programmatic configuration management and must follow any platform naming conventions for system-wide entries.

value.description:
Optional filter for the setting's value.

Acceptable values are plain strings or valid JSON-encoded policy data, as stored in the 'value' column of the discussion_board_system_settings table. Large or complex value patterns (including escaped JSON or encoded arrays) may affect backend search or audit performance. Field respects any max length or pattern constraints defined in the database schema.

Intended to help operators search for settings by content, policy, or technical parameters.

description.description:
Optional filter for the system setting's administrative description.

This field allows operators to audit or locate configuration items by their long-form human-readable business context. Serves for documentation, auditing, or operator notes. Intended as a flexible text field; may be omitted, short, or contain operator best practices for discovery and auditing workflows.

page.description: The page number for paginated results. Defaults to 1 if not specified. Used by administrators to page through large sets of configuration entries.

limit.description: The maximum number of results to return per page. Helps administrators manage result sizes for large policy tables and audits.

oneOf.description: Sorts the results by the specified setting column. Allowed values are: 'key', 'value', 'created_at', and 'updated_at'. Used to prioritize review or audit workflow.

sort_key.description: Sorts the results by the specified setting column. Allowed values are: 'key', 'value', 'created_at', and 'updated_at'. Used to prioritize review or audit workflow.

oneOf.description: Direction in which to sort the results: 'asc' for ascending, 'desc' for descending. Enables administrators to control review or audit order.
Direction in which to sort the results: 'asc' for ascending, 'desc' for descending. Enables administrators to control review or audit order.

sort_direction.description: Direction in which to sort the results: 'asc' for ascending, 'desc' for descending. Enables administrators to control review or audit order.

IDiscussionBoardSystemSetting.IRequest.description:
Request parameters for searching and filtering system settings in the discussion board platform.

Supports filtering by configuration key (which must match the unique key in discussion_board_system_settings), value (with string or valid JSON semantics), or description (admin/operator documentation). Paginates and sorts the result list for efficient review and audit. All field descriptions enhanced and cross-referenced with underlying Prisma model and API operational constraints.

id.description: Primary Key for the system settings entry. Identifies the unique configuration record within the discussion_board_system_settings table and supports programmatic management and audit tracking.

key.description: Unique identifier for this configuration setting or policy entry. Used throughout the system to reference and update specific settings programmatically. Enforced as globally unique by the Prisma schema.

value.description: Value for this system setting. May encode raw value, serialized JSON, or application-specific policy text. Determines the effect of this system setting throughout the platform.

description.description: Optional human-readable explanation or policy summary for this setting. Enables documentation and contextual understanding of the configuration entry's business purpose.

created_at.description: Timestamp for creation of this settings entry. Allows administrators to audit when the configuration was established. Follows ISO 8601 format.

updated_at.description: Timestamp for last update or modification of this settings entry. Used for audit trails and determining the latest system state.

oneOf.description: Soft deletion timestamp for audit and rollback; null unless marked for deletion. Field is null when the setting is active.

deleted_at.description: Soft deletion timestamp for audit and rollback; null unless marked for deletion. Field is null when the setting is active.

IDiscussionBoardSystemSetting.description:
Discussion board platform system-level configuration entry.

Represents a key/value-based setting that controls platform-wide business, technical, or operational policies. Each setting is uniquely identified by its 'key' and supports extensive documentation, audit trails, and soft-deletion tracking. Designed for use by administrators in centralized configuration and policy management workflows.

key.description: Unique identifier for this configuration setting or policy entry. Used to retrieve or update specific settings programmatically. Follows the unique constraint of the discussion_board_system_settings table and MUST NOT duplicate any existing key.

value.description: Value for this system setting. May encode a raw value, serialized JSON object, or application-specific policy text. Required when creating new settings.

description.description: Optional human-readable explanation or policy summary for this setting. Useful for administrators or operators to document the setting's purpose. Nullable if not supplied during creation.

IDiscussionBoardSystemSetting.ICreate.description:
Payload for creating a new system-wide configuration setting in the discussion_board_system_settings table.

Includes a unique 'key', required 'value', and an optional 'description'. Follows the business constraint that 'key' is globally unique. Intended for use by admins to programmably add policies, feature toggles, or infrastructure configurations for the discussion board platform.

All entries are tracked for auditing, with initial timestamps automatically set by the server on creation.

value.description: Updated value for this system setting. May encode a raw value, serialized JSON, or application-specific policy text. Only value and/or description may be updated; key is immutable.

description.description: Optional updated human-readable documentation for this setting's purpose or policy intent. Can be set to null to clear it, or omitted to leave unchanged.

IDiscussionBoardSystemSetting.IUpdate.description:
Payload to update an existing system-wide configuration setting in the discussion_board_system_settings table, referenced by its 'key' path parameter.

Only 'value' and/or 'description' may be changed; the 'key' is immutable and must not be included in the payload. At least one property (value or description) SHOULD be supplied per update. This structure is intended for administrative use in amending platform-wide policies, technical parameters, or audit notes. All changes update audit metadata.

IDiscussionBoardUser.IRequest.description:
Search and filter criteria for finding and paginating discussion board user accounts. Includes registration window, account status, verification, and related filters.

Enables administrator control over user listing queries, including filtering by registration date, email match, user status (active/blocked), and verification flags. Supports advanced search for robust user management and compliance reporting.

email.description: Optional filter for the user's email address to find accounts matching or containing the specified value. Enables precise or fuzzy search on login email for administrative auditing.

is_active.description: Optional filter for user activation status. If set, only users matching the active/inactive state will be included in search results.

is_blocked.description: Optional filter for blocked user status. If provided, enables targeted browsing of blocked or non-blocked user accounts to support moderation workflows.

is_email_verified.description: Optional filter by email verification status. Limiting to verified/unverified users allows compliance and onboarding tracking.

created_from.description: Optional registration window start (inclusive). Only users created on or after this timestamp will be included in the search. ISO 8601 date-time format.

created_to.description: Optional registration window end (inclusive). Only users created on or before this timestamp are included. Supports auditing users registered within a specific date range. ISO 8601.

deleted.description: If true, include only users who are soft deleted (deleted_at != null). If false, include only users who are NOT soft deleted. If omitted, both deleted and non-deleted users may be included.

page.description: Pagination start, 1-based index for fetching result pages. Used together with limit to navigate through large result sets.

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return per page (pagination size). Common admin UIs use 10, 20, 50, or 100 as options.

oneOf.description: Sort field for ordering the result set. Supported values: created_at, email.
Sort field for ordering the result set. Supported values: created_at, email.

order_by.description: Sort field for ordering the result set. Supported values: created_at, email.

oneOf.description: Sort direction for ordering results. Ascending or descending.
Sort direction for ordering results. Ascending or descending.

order_dir.description: Sort direction for ordering results. Ascending or descending.

IDiscussionBoardUser.description:
User accounts for platform participants.

Represents each registered end-user on the discussion board. Contains identity fields for login, authentication, account status, and minimal profile information. Every user may have multiple concurrent active sessions tracked in the discussion_board_user_sessions table. Business logic ensures email is unique for secure login. Temporal fields enable soft deletion and audit trails. Fields facilitate account recovery and future extensibility for additional user profile attributes.

Relations to administrator oversight (discussion_board_admins) and session management are fundamental for secure platform governance.

id.description: Primary key. Universally unique identifier for the user.

email.description: User's email address for login and notification purposes. Must be unique. Used for authentication and password recovery.

is_email_verified.description: Indicates whether the user's email address has been verified. Email verification is required before participation.

is_active.description: Denotes if the user account is active and allowed to log in. Blocked users have this set to false.

is_blocked.description: Indicates if the user is blocked for rule violations. Blocked users cannot log in or participate until reactivated.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the user account was created.

updated_at.description: Timestamp when the user account was last updated.

oneOf.description: Optional timestamp for soft deletion. If set, the account is considered deleted but can be restored.

deleted_at.description: Optional timestamp for soft deletion. If set, the account is considered deleted but can be restored.

IDiscussionBoardUser.IUpdate.description:
Update DTO for discussion board user accounts.

This schema defines the subset of user account fields that may be modified by administrators through the update user endpoint. It is used for administrator-initiated updates of user state (active, blocked), email address, and email verification status. System-generated fields, primary keys, and authentication context fields are excluded. Only business-updatable properties are present. All updates trigger business logic for account audit, email uniqueness, and may induce security events such as re-verification or account restoration.

This DTO enforces policy that user status change, email update, and verification can only be performed by admins and are subject to business validation rules. Ownership and identity fields are immutable and not updatable by this DTO.

email.description: User's email address to update. Must remain unique within the platform. Triggers re-verification or notification upon change if business workflow requires. Optional for partial update.

is_email_verified.description: Set to true to mark the user's email as verified (usually by admin after appropriate verification or compliance checks). Optional for partial update.

is_active.description: Set to true to activate the user account, or false to deactivate (block login and participation). Optional for partial update. Business rules ensure that activating/deactivating an account may have compliance, notification, or logging effects.

is_blocked.description: Set to true to block a user for rule violations; false to unblock. Optional for partial update. Blocking may trigger user notification, audit log, and session revocation.

IDiscussionBoardUserSession.IRequest.description:
Request DTO for searching and filtering user session records (discussion_board_user_sessions) related to a specific user.

Provides complex filtering, pagination, sorting, and search criteria for retrieving a paginated list of session summaries for a user. Used exclusively by admin endpoints as the request body for session listing. Enables audits of login activity, security investigation, and administrative review. Includes standard pagination parameters (page, pageSize), and may include filters such as date range, session expiration status, or IP address.

Standard business rules require that only authorized admins can execute search/filter queries for user session history. Filtering by userId is not included (provided by path context).

page.description: Pagination: 1-based page number of session records to return.

pageSize.description: Pagination: number of session summary records per page (max 100 per request).

createdFrom.description: Filter: only include sessions created at or after this ISO 8601 date/time value.

createdTo.description: Filter: only include sessions created at or before this ISO 8601 date/time value.

expired.description: Filter: limit results to expired or active (non-expired) sessions only. Null for no filter.

ip.description: Filter: restrict sessions to those initiated from this IP address. May be null for no filter.

id.description: Primary key for the user session. Universally unique identifier for each login session, enabling accurate distinction and retrieval for audit or administrative review.

discussion_board_user_id.description: Reference to the associated user account. Foreign key to discussion_board_users.id, ensuring linkage from this session to the owning end user for platform participant traceability.

ip.description: IP address from which the session was initiated. Used for audit purposes and security monitoring.

href.description: URL from which the login or session was established. Tracks originating point for user access context.

referrer.description: HTTP referrer value at the start of the session. Captures the web address or context which led to the session being initiated.

created_at.description: Time the session was created. Represents when the user authenticated or began the session.

expired_at.description: Time the session expired or ended. Nullable – is null when the session is still active or if expiry was never recorded.

IDiscussionBoardUserSession.description: Discussion board user session record. Represents a single user login session for audit and platform security. Stores contextual metadata including originating IP, URL context, HTTP referrer, creation and optional expiration times. Each session is associated with one user in the discussion_board_users table. Sessions are read by privileged users for platform security and administration. All data fields are retrieved directly from the database.

email.description: Filter for administrator accounts by exact email address. Allows precise searching for admins with a specific login email. If omitted, search includes any email address.

is_email_verified.description: Search filter to restrict results to admins with verified (true) or unverified (false) email addresses. If omitted, both statuses are included.

is_active.description: Search filter for admin accounts that are active (true) or inactive (false). If not specified, returns both active and inactive admins.

is_blocked.description: Restrict results to blocked (true) or unblocked (false) admins. Allows enforcement of account status queries.

created_from.description: Lower bound for admin account creation timestamp. Returns only admins created at or after this time. Must be in ISO8601 date-time format. If omitted, no lower bound is applied.

created_to.description: Upper bound for admin account creation timestamp. Returns only admins created before or at this time. Must be in ISO8601 date-time format. If omitted, no upper bound is applied.

page.description: Pagination: page number of the result set, starting from 1.

page_size.description: Number of admin accounts to return per page. Must be positive integer.

oneOf.description: Sort results by either admin account creation time or email address. Supported values are 'created_at' (default) or 'email'.
Sort results by either admin account creation time or email address. Supported values are 'created_at' (default) or 'email'.

order_by.description: Sort results by either admin account creation time or email address. Supported values are 'created_at' (default) or 'email'.

oneOf.description: Sort order direction. Use 'asc' for ascending or 'desc' for descending order. Default is 'desc' (most recent first).
Sort order direction. Use 'asc' for ascending or 'desc' for descending order. Default is 'desc' (most recent first).

order_direction.description: Sort order direction. Use 'asc' for ascending or 'desc' for descending order. Default is 'desc' (most recent first).

IDiscussionBoardAdmin.IRequest.description: Request schema for searching, filtering, and paginating discussion board administrator accounts. Supports search on core admin fields, filter by status and verification, and flexible sorting/pagination. Used only by platform administrators and privileged operators for oversight and audit.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the admin.

Primary key, UUID format, used for all platform-wide reference and audit activities.

email.description:
Admin's unique email address used for login and communication.

This must be unique across all admin records and is the basis for authentication and platform communication.

is_email_verified.description:
Indicates if the admin's email address has been verified.

Used to enforce security policies, enhanced platform privileges rely on a verified email address.

is_active.description:
True if the admin account is active and enabled for moderation activity.

Deactivated accounts remain in the database but cannot log in or use admin features.

is_blocked.description:
True if the admin is suspended or blocked from accessing admin features.

Blocked status may be used for temporary suspensions or as the result of moderation investigations.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the admin account was created.

Non-null, managed by the platform and used for audit and compliance.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp of the last update to the admin's profile or status.

Updated automatically on any profile/status change for traceability.

deleted_at.description:
Timestamp of soft deletion; nullable if the account is not deleted.

Soft deleted accounts remain available for audit and compliance investigation, but are concealed from normal admin lists.

IDiscussionBoardAdmin.description:
Administrator accounts for platform oversight and moderation.

Represents admin user records with full credential, verification, and status information. Excludes password_hash and any sensitive authentication fields from API responses. Every admin can be uniquely referenced by id and email, features status flags for platform, and tracks audit fields for creation, update, and soft deletion.

This type is returned in admin detail queries and update operations, supporting privileged platform audit, management, and oversight workflows.

email.description:
Admin's unique email address.

To update login/email address, must remain unique across all admin records.

password.description:
Plain text password to be securely updated. The backend will hash and store it in the 'password_hash' field in Prisma.

This field MUST be provided as plain text; never allow pre-hashed passwords via API. Passwords must adhere to platform policy for length and complexity.

is_email_verified.description:
Whether email of the admin is verified.

If set true, enables privileged admin actions. Used for platform security control.

is_active.description:
Account status flag (active/inactive).

Active admins have access to all moderation and oversight features. Inactive admins are blocked from logging in.

is_blocked.description:
Block/suspension flag for privilege enforcement.

If true, admin cannot log in or perform any moderator features until status is cleared by operators.

IDiscussionBoardAdmin.IUpdate.description:
Payload for updating administrator accounts.

All fields are required to ensure full credential and status synchronization. Most sensitive fields, such as 'password', are provided only in trusted operator contexts and never exposed in API responses. Provide the full set of status toggles to handle changes in access, verification, and blocking in a single privileged operation. The request body must satisfy all schema constraints before update is applied.

id.description: Primary key. Universally unique identifier for the admin session.

discussion_board_admin_id.description: Reference to the associated admin account. Points to discussion_board_admins.id.

ip.description: Network IP address for this moderation session.

href.description: URL at start of session or moderation activity.

referrer.description: Referrer value for admin connection context.

created_at.description: Session creation time.

expired_at.description: Session end time, nullable until expired.

IDiscussionBoardAdminSession.description:
Administrator session record representing an authentication and moderation audit event for an admin. Contains linkage to the corresponding admin, connection context (IP, URL, referrer), creation time, and optional expiration time.

This entity is essential for tracking, auditing, and securing admin-level actions within the discussion board platform. Follows the Prisma session schema for full compliance and reliability. All business logic for session lifecycle, linkage, and expiry is based on this structure.

page.description: Page number for paginated admin session listing.

limit.description: Page size limit for admin session pagination (max 100).

oneOf.description: Field by which to sort session results.
Field by which to sort session results.

sort_by.description: Field by which to sort session results.

oneOf.description: Sort order (ascending or descending) for listed sessions.
Sort order (ascending or descending) for listed sessions.

order.description: Sort order (ascending or descending) for listed sessions.

IDiscussionBoardAdminSession.IRequest.description:
Request parameters for paginating, filtering, and sorting administrator session records. Used in the PATCH /admins/{adminId}/sessions endpoint to traverse or search session logs.

Pagination (page, limit) is business-constrained; sorting by creation or expiration timestamp is allowed. All request logic is compatible with the discussion_board_admin_sessions schema and the session listing API specification.

IDiscussionBoardArticle.IRequest.description: Request filter, search, sorting, and pagination parameters used when searching for discussion board articles. Supports advanced searching by title/body keyword, author information (user/admin), or temporal range. Options exist for sort order by created_at, relevance, or popularity. Enables efficient navigation through large content sets, including complex combinations supported by business use cases.

keyword.description: Search keyword to match in the article's title or body content. Used for full-text search queries. Optional, but recommended for user-driven searches.

author_user_id.description: Restrict search results to articles authored by a specific user by their user UUID. Optional parameter. If provided, only articles by this user will be returned.

author_admin_id.description: Restrict search results to articles authored by a specific admin by their admin UUID. Optional parameter. If provided, only articles by this admin will be returned.

created_from.description: Filter articles created at or after this timestamp. Useful for searching recent discussions.

created_until.description: Filter articles created at or before this timestamp. Used for historical or archival searches.

is_active.description: Filter by active (non-deleted) articles only. If true, returns only articles without deleted_at set. If false, can include or exclusively return soft-deleted articles depending on business use case.

oneOf.description: Sorting criterion for result order. Allowed values: created_at (chronological), relevance (search match score), popularity (engagement measures).
Sorting criterion for result order. Allowed values: created_at (chronological), relevance (search match score), popularity (engagement measures).
