page.description: Which page of results to return. 1-based indexing. Defaults to 1 if not provided.

limit.description: Maximum items per page. Hard limit at 100 for performance. Defaults to system policy if omitted.

IDiscussionBoardArticle.description:
Discussion board article representing a single post for economic or political debate. Primary content created by users or admins. Includes title, body, author attribution, creation and update timestamps. Relations include user or admin author, file/image attachments, and versioning snapshots for edit/audit trail.

Each article has an optional author_user_id (points to a user) or author_admin_id (points to an admin) for provenance. Parent-child relationships to attachments and snapshots enable advanced discussion and moderation features. Soft deletion via deleted_at is enforced for compliance and recoverability.

The article entity is immutable regarding author relationship after creation; only title, body, and soft-deletion are changeable. Attachments and snapshots provide composition and audit trail (not returned directly in this DTO; use separate endpoints for those).

Returned in detail responses for article view, update, and deletion endpoints.

id.description: Primary key. Unique article identifier.

title.description: Article headline. Must be between 5 and 150 characters as enforced by business rules.

body.description: Main content of the article. Must be between 20 and 5000 characters by business specification. Markdown formatting may be supported, but is stored as plain text.

author_user.description: Embedded summary of the user who authored this article. Null if the article was created by an admin author.

author_admin.description: Embedded summary of the admin who authored this article. Null if the article was created by a user author.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the article was created.

updated_at.description: Timestamp when the article was last updated.

IDiscussionBoardUser.ISummary.description:
Summary view of a registered user on the discussion board platform.

Used for list displays, reference relations, or lightweight identity contexts. Represents minimal profile and status information about an end-user while ensuring security and privacy boundaries are enforced.

Fields reflect core business logic: unique login, user authentication, account status, and soft deletion audit trail.

id.description: Universally unique identifier for the user. Primary key in the user database table.

email.description: Unique email address used for authentication and communication. Used for login and notification delivery.

is_email_verified.description: Indicates whether this user's email address has been verified. Email verification is required for participation and business operations.

is_active.description: Account activation status. true if the user is allowed to log in and use the platform; false if the account is currently disabled.

is_blocked.description: true if the account is blocked due to rule violations or moderation actions. A blocked user cannot log in or access board functions.

created_at.description: Timestamp of user account creation. Used for audit trails and sorting.

updated_at.description: Timestamp of last update to this user's data.

deleted_at.description: Timestamp of soft deletion. Nullable; present only if the account is considered deleted, for recovery and audit.

IDiscussionBoardAdmin.ISummary.description:
Summary information about a platform administrator who can perform moderation or audit actions.

This object is intended for embedding in moderation logs and events to provide user-facing context for audit trails.

Typically includes only essential identity and display information, not sensitive profile details.

id.description: Unique identifier for the administrator account.

display_name.description: Human-readable display name of the administrator. Used in moderation logs and audit records.

IDiscussionBoardArticle.ICreate.description:
Data structure for creating a new discussion board article in the economic or political debate platform.

Contains all fields needed for initial article insertion, subject to business validation rules. The title field must be between 5 and 150 characters, and the body must be between 20 and 5000 characters based on requirements. Author context (user or admin attribution) is handled by backend authentication; the DTO excludes direct author ID input for security and traceability. Attachments and moderation are supported via separate flows, not included here.

Upon successful validation, the system will timestamp creation and persist the article with all metadata defined in the underlying Prisma 'discussion_board_articles' model.

Used in POST /discussionBoard/user/articles and similar endpoints for both user and admin submission flows.

title.description: Article headline. Must be between 5 and 150 characters. Required for all discussion board articles.

body.description: Main content of the article. Must be between 20 and 5000 characters according to platform rules.

IDiscussionBoardArticle.IUpdate.description:
DTO for updating an existing article in the discussion board. Allows modification of the title and/or body based on permission and business rules.

The update operation must conform to length constraints: title requires 5-150 characters, body requires 20-5000 characters. Author context and owner-only restrictions are managed via backend authentication and authorization; the DTO does not permit changes to author fields. Updates are audit-trailed using snapshot and moderation tables for compliance.

At least one of title or body must be provided for a valid update. Use in PUT /discussionBoard/user/articles/{articleId} and /discussionBoard/admin/articles/{articleId}.

title.description: New headline for the article. Must be 5 to 150 characters if provided. Update is optional, but one of title or body is required.

body.description: Updated main content. Must be 20 to 5000 characters if supplied. At least one of title or body must appear in an update request.

IDiscussionBoardArticleAttachment.IReque.description:
Request parameters for searching and paginating attachments associated with a specific article in the discussion board. Supports filter by file name (full-text indexing), MIME type, and upload date range. Pagination and sorting allow for scalable querying of large attachment collections.

Each request operates within the context of a parent article and should include only those filters relevant to user search needs within that article. This type ensures request compatibility with both basic and advanced attachment listing UIs on the platform. The file name filter supports partial and full-text match by leveraging Postgres index on file_name.

file_name.description: Optional: Filter attachments by matching (partial or full-text) original filename. Supports evidence discovery and rapid searching within large attachment sets.

file_type.description: Optional: Filter attachments by MIME type, e.g. 'image/png', 'application/pdf'. Enables refinement of search to specific file classes.

uploaded_date_start.description: Optional: Lower bound (inclusive) for filtering by upload timestamp. Used when searching for attachments uploaded after a given moment. RFC 3339 format.

uploaded_date_end.description: Optional: Upper bound (inclusive) for filtering by upload timestamp. Useful for finding only recently added files. RFC 3339 format.

page.description: Pagination page number (1-based). Optional, defaults to 1 if not provided.

limit.description: Pagination page size (number of attachments per page). Optional, defaults to service-defined limit if not specified.

IDiscussionBoardArticleAttachment.description:
Represents an attachment (file or image) associated with a specific discussion board article. Includes storage URI, file name, MIME type, file size, upload timestamp, and article reference.

Attachments enable users to supplement article content with supporting evidence. Each attachment record is tied to a single article and is removed if the parent article is deleted. Metadata fields such as file_name, file_type, file_size, and uploaded_at facilitate search, preview, download, and moderation workflows. The storage URI provides the backend location of the file for secure retrieval.

References to the article are made by UUID, ensuring uniqueness and integrity. The model is enforced by business rules regarding allowed file types and maximum size.

id.description: Unique identifier for the attachment.

article_id.description: Reference to the article this attachment belongs to. Corresponds to discussion_board_articles.id.

uri.description: Storage URI for the actual attachment file or image. Used for secure retrieval from backend storage.

file_name.description: Original filename of the uploaded attachment. Used for display and evidence tracking.

file_type.description: MIME type of the attachment, e.g., 'image/png', 'application/pdf'. Enforced on upload and used for type filtering.

file_size.description: Size of the attachment in bytes. Must not exceed 10MB as per business rule. Used for validations and display.

uploaded_at.description: Timestamp when this attachment was uploaded. Used for searching, sorting, and auditing.

uri.description: Storage URI for the file or image attachment. This must point to a pre-uploaded file in backend storage. Required for attachment creation and always validated against allowed URI patterns. The file must already be uploaded before attachment registration.

file_name.description: Original filename of the uploaded attachment. The name is used for display and audit purposes. File naming is subject to business logic validation and cannot be empty.

file_type.description: MIME type of the attachment, such as 'image/png', 'application/pdf', etc. Only allowed file types defined in business logic may be uploaded.

file_size.description: Size of the attachment in bytes. Maximum allowed is 10MB, checked in business logic. Must be a positive integer and reflects the actual uploaded file size.

IDiscussionBoardArticleAttachment.ICreat.description:
Create DTO for registering a new attachment (image or document) to a discussion board article.

Allows an authenticated user (usually the article's author or an admin) to add a supporting file or image to an article. The client must pre-upload the file and provide its storage URI, checked for compliance with allowed patterns. Metadata including original filename, file type, and file size are captured for audit and display.

Parent article reference is implicit via the API path and must not be set directly in the request body. Attachment creation is subject to business validation rules for type, size, and total allowed attachments per article.

file_name.description: Original filename of the uploaded attachment. Allows updating the name for display or clarification purposes. The new name must follow all business logic rules and cannot be empty.

file_type.description: MIME type of the attachment, such as 'image/png', 'application/pdf', etc. Updating the file type is typically used for correction purposes but must match allowed values.

IDiscussionBoardArticleAttachment.IUpdat.description:
Update DTO for modifying the metadata of an existing article attachment.

Enables authorized users (attachment owner or admin) to change the filename or file type associated with the attachment, but not the storage URI or the parent article reference. Only mutable fields are editable. Business rules validate the new name and type for safety and compliance.

All operations are audit-logged, and invalid updates (e.g., attempting to change non-editable fields) are rejected. Used in PUT operations for attachments.

IDiscussionBoardArticleSnapshot.description:
Historical snapshot of a discussion board article state, captured for versioning and audit purposes.

Each snapshot stores the article's title, body, author user (or admin) at a given edit point in time. Used to support a complete edit history for compliance and moderation. Snapshots are immutable and created by system logic when articles are edited. Instead of referencing authors by UUIDs, this structure provides full author context via `.ISummary` objects for both user and admin.

article_id remains a scalar as the hierarchical parent.

This allows for atomic retrieval of all auditing and author context with no N+1 query problem.

In addition, to maintain referential integrity and enable traceable audit logs, the snapshot record also includes the author_user_id and author_admin_id fields. These are stored as nullable UUIDs and enable database-level connection to the original author identity even in scenarios where the summary object cannot be reconstructed, such as after user or admin deletion. This supports robust audit trails for regulatory, compliance, and moderation workflows.

id.description: Unique identifier for this snapshot record. Primary key for the snapshot in the audit log table.

article_id.description: Reference to the article whose state this snapshot records. Links to discussion_board_articles.id.

author_user_id.description: Reference to the user author at the time of this snapshot. Points to discussion_board_users.id. Nullable, present only if authored by user. Enables referential trace and audit even if author context is subsequently deleted.

author_admin_id.description: Reference to the admin author at the time of this snapshot. Points to discussion_board_admins.id. Nullable, present only if authored/modified by admin. Facilitates moderation audit trails for post creation or editing by staff.

author_user.description: Complete user context for the author at the time of this snapshot, or null if authored/edited by admin. Uses IDiscussionBoardUser.ISummary.

author_admin.description: Complete admin context for the author at the time of this snapshot, or null if authored/edited by user. Uses IDiscussionBoardAdmin.ISummary.

title.description: Snapshot of the article title at the exact edit event.

body.description: Snapshot of the article content at snapshot creation.

created_at.description: Time at which this snapshot was created.

IDiscussionBoardArticleSnapshot.IRequest.description:
Query/filter options for searching or paginating through article snapshots belonging to a specific article.

Supports filtering by date range, authorship (user/admin), and sorting/pagination for audit trail review. Used by PATCH endpoints to return paginated and filtered snapshot lists for a given article ID.

oneOf.description: Filter: Only include snapshots created after this time.

start_date.description: Optional filter. Only include snapshots created at or after this date. ISO8601 format. If omitted, no lower bound.

oneOf.description: Filter: Only include snapshots created before this time.

end_date.description: Optional filter. Only include snapshots created at or before this date. ISO8601 format. If omitted, no upper bound.

oneOf.description: If present, only include snapshots authored by users or admins as specified.
If present, only include snapshots authored by users or admins as specified.

author_type.description: Optional filter. If set to 'user', only include user-authored snapshots. If set to 'admin', only include admin-authored.

oneOf.description: Filter: Only include snapshots authored by this user/admin (matches both user and admin authorship IDs).

author_id.description: Optional filter: return only snapshots by a specific user or admin author. Allows more granular audit search.

page.description: Pagination: page number (1-based). Required for cursor/offset-based pagination.

limit.description: Maximum number of snapshot records per page. Defaults to system standard if not set.

oneOf.description: Sorts by creation time ascending (oldest first) or descending (most recent first, default).
Sorts by creation time ascending (oldest first) or descending (most recent first, default).

sort_order.description: Sort order for snapshot creation time. 'desc' returns most recent first. If omitted, defaults to 'desc'.

IDiscussionBoardComment.IRequest.description:
Search, filtering, and pagination criteria for retrieving a collection of comments from the discussion board.

Allows clients to filter comments by article, author (user or admin), keywords, and creation/update date ranges. Provides parameters for advanced moderation, analytics, or user browsing scenarios. Pagination and sorting fields enable efficient browsing of large comment datasets. Only non-soft-deleted comments should be returned by default unless otherwise specified.

article_id.description: Unique identifier of the discussion board article to filter comments by. When omitted, comments from all articles are included.

author_user_id.description: Unique identifier of the user author to filter comments by. If specified, only comments authored by this user are included.

author_admin_id.description: Unique identifier of the admin author to filter comments by. If specified, only comments authored by this admin are included.

content_keywords.description: Search keyword(s) to filter comments by body content. Matches substrings or keyword patterns in the text body. Optional.

created_from.description: Lower bound (inclusive) for comment creation date filtering. Only comments created after this timestamp (ISO 8601) are included.

created_to.description: Upper bound (inclusive) for comment creation date filtering. Only comments created before this timestamp (ISO 8601) are included.

updated_from.description: Lower bound (inclusive) for comment last update date filtering. Only comments updated after this timestamp are included.

updated_to.description: Upper bound (inclusive) for comment last update date filtering. Only comments updated before this timestamp are included.

page.description: Current result page index (1-based). Defaults to 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of comments per result page. Enforces upper bound of 100 for performance. Defaults to 20.

oneOf.description: Field to sort the results by. Accepts 'created_at' (default) or 'updated_at'.
Field to sort the results by. Accepts 'created_at' (default) or 'updated_at'.

sort_by.description: Field to sort the results by. Accepts 'created_at' (default) or 'updated_at'.

oneOf.description: Sort direction to order results: ascending (asc) or descending (desc). Defaults to 'desc' for newest comments first.
Sort direction to order results: ascending (asc) or descending (desc). Defaults to 'desc' for newest comments first.

sort_direction.description: Sort direction to order results: ascending (asc) or descending (desc). Defaults to 'desc' for newest comments first.

IDiscussionBoardComment.description:
Represents a comment on a discussion board article.

Each comment belongs to a specific article and is authored by either a user or an administrator. Comments include content, audit fields, soft deletion status, and provide full context for both article and author via summary types. This response also lists any files/images attached to the comment, with business rules enforcing a maximum of 2 attachments per comment (see: attachments field). Attachments are surfaced as an array of summary DTOs (IDiscussionBoardCommentAttachment.ISummary).

Attachments are associated via a separate endpoint for creation, but always returned as part of the comment for complete business context. API clients should expect the attachments field to be present and to enforce client-side attachment count and display logic. This resolves previous ambiguity regarding the linkage between comments and their attachments, ensuring API consumers always see attachment information in the canonical comment response object.

id.description: Unique identifier for the comment.

article.description: Summary context of the article this comment belongs to.

author.description: Contextual summary of the comment author, discriminated between user (regular member) or admin. Always present with type appropriate to authorship.

body.description: Text content of the comment. Required.

attachments.description: List of attachments—files or images—associated with this comment. Maximum 2 attachments allowed per comment. Attachments are always returned here in the comment response object for business context and UI rendering. Each attachment contains metadata including filename, MIME type, URL, and additional moderation or auditing data as per attachment summary DTO definition.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the comment was created.

updated_at.description: Timestamp when the comment was last updated.

IDiscussionBoardComment.ICreate.description:
Data required to create a new comment on a discussion board article.

This type is used to submit commentary from a registered user or admin linked to a given article on the board. It enforces business validation of content (2–1000 characters), ensures authorship attribution by current actor (user or admin), and establishes association to the parent article. Optionally accepts up to 2 file attachments via subsidiary attachment DTOs. System-managed fields like timestamps and actor IDs are handled by the server and excluded from the request body.

Attachments, if provided, must follow allowed file type and size rules (max 10MB per file), and all relationships are checked for integrity upon creation.

discussion_board_article_id.description: The UUID of the target article this comment is for. Required. The parent article must exist.

body.description: Comment text content, 2 to 1000 characters as per business constraints and moderation needs.

attachments.description: Optional array of up to 2 file/image attachments for this comment (max 10MB each). Attachments must be valid file URLs. If omitted, the comment will have no attachments.

file_url.description:
Storage location URI for the attachment file.

Must be a valid URI string, representing the location of the uploaded file or image in external storage (e.g., S3, CDN).
This URI is used for secure download access after upload and is validated according to platform security policies.

original_filename.description:
The filename as originally uploaded by the user.

Serves as the user-facing display name for the file. Must not be empty and must meet allowed naming conventions and file name length restrictions set by platform policy. Duplicate filenames within the same comment are not permitted (see database unique constraint).

mime_type.description:
MIME type of the attachment (e.g., 'image/png', 'application/pdf').

Must be provided by the client and represent a supported document or image type for comment attachments. Valid MIME types are enforced by business validation logic. Required for download/content negotiation and moderation.

file_size_bytes.description:
The file size in bytes. Must be between 1 byte and 10 megabytes (10,485,760 bytes), enforced by validation before attachment record creation.

This value is used for storage accounting, frontend size checks, and to disallow overly large attachments. Zero-byte or negative file sizes are not allowed.

IDiscussionBoardCommentAttachment.ICreat.description:
Attachment data and metadata for associating a new file or image with a discussion board comment.

Used as the request body for creating a new comment attachment. Contains information necessary for business and security validation (file URI, name, type, and size). All fields are mandatory. Duplicate filenames on the same comment are not allowed by unique index on (discussion_board_comment_id, original_filename).

The file must be uploaded separately and a valid file URL included here.

Direct mapping to Prisma model: discussion_board_comment_attachments (except for parent comment ID, which is supplied via path param, not body).

IDiscussionBoardComment.IUpdate.description:
Data required to update an existing discussion board comment.

Allows the comment owner (user or admin) or an authorized moderator to revise the body content of an active (non-deleted) comment. The body is subject to the same validation and length limits as during creation (2–1000 characters). Attachment management is performed through a separate endpoint and is not available within this operation. This DTO focuses on comment text and is not permitted to alter authorship, parent article association, or system-managed fields like timestamps or deletion state.

body.description: Updated comment text content, must be between 2 and 1000 characters per moderation rules and validation.

IDiscussionBoardCommentAttachment.description:
Represents a file or image attached to a comment on the discussion board.

Each IDiscussionBoardCommentAttachment record links a single file or image to one parent comment via a foreign key. This object is used to manage comment attachment uploads (maximum two attachments per comment) and tracks all metadata necessary for download authorization, moderation, and auditing.

Attachment entities are always dependent on their parent comment and are deleted if the parent is deleted. Important metadata includes the storage URI, original filename, MIME type, file size, and creation timestamp. File uploads are validated for allowed types and size (max 10MB). The object enforces unique filename constraints within a given comment and should not be used to serve actual file content (only metadata).

Used in API responses for retrieving single attachment metadata as well as when creating or updating attachments.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the attachment.

This is the system-generated primary key for the attachment record, following UUID format. Used to reference the attachment in API operations and enforce uniqueness.

discussion_board_comment_id.description:
References the parent comment to which this attachment belongs.

Foreign key relation to the discussion_board_comments table. Attachments are always dependent on their parent and are cascade-deleted if the parent is deleted.

file_url.description:
Storage URI for the attachment file.

This is the location of the file in the storage backend (e.g., S3 URI or CDN link). Used to retrieve the file content, but actual file serving is handled by a different API or direct download mechanism. Always validated to be a proper URI string.

original_filename.description:
Original filename as uploaded by the user.

Used for display, auditing, and enforcing uniqueness (filename must be unique per comment).

mime_type.description:
MIME type for the attachment (e.g., image/png, application/pdf).

Indicates the type of file uploaded and is validated both by API logic and client submission.

file_size_bytes.description:
File size in bytes.

Used for business validation: attachments must not exceed 10MB (10,485,760 bytes). This field enables storage cost calculations, moderation, and front-end file restrictions.

created_at.description:
Attachment creation/upload timestamp.

Records the UTC time when the attachment was created. Used in moderation/auditing and to support chronological display or sorting.

IDiscussionBoardCommentAttachment.IReque.description:
Query and filter parameters for retrieving a paginated list of attachments associated with a specific comment.

Used in PATCH operations on endpoints to retrieve search results for attachments filtered by filename, MIME type, creation date, and with support for pagination and sorting. Allows clients to customize listing behaviors for large boards or comment threads and supports moderation workflows.

All filters are optional; results are always scoped to the parent comment identified by path parameter. Pagination enables efficient browsing of comments with many attachments.

original_filename.description:
Wildcard or exact match for the original uploaded filename.

Used to filter the attachment list to only show files matching the supplied (partial) filename. Useful for moderation or search and accepts partial matches.

mime_type.description:
Filter for attachments matching a given MIME type.

Allows selection of attachments with a specific type, e.g., image/jpeg or application/pdf. Useful for filtering to images only, PDFs, etc.

created_before.description:
Upper bound timestamp for returned attachments.

Only attachments created before this UTC date-time are included in the results. Used for date-based searching, moderation, or archival scenarios.

created_after.description:
Lower bound timestamp for returned attachments.

Attachments created on or after this UTC date-time will be included. Helpful for searching recent uploads or filtering time windows.

limit.description:
Pagination: maximum number of attachments to return in this page of results.

Typical values might be 10 or 20. Defaults should be enforced by API layer. Used to control result set size and page efficiently through large datasets.

offset.description:
Pagination offset for result list.

Specifies the number of records to skip before returning results (for paginated results sets). Combined with limit, supports efficient browsing through attachments.

sort_by.description:
Sort field for returned attachments.

Indicates which property of the attachment (e.g., created_at, original_filename, file_size_bytes) to use for ordering results. The allowed values should be enforced by API implementation.

sort_order.description:
Sorting order for the attachment list, either ascending or descending.

Allowed values: "asc" for ascending, "desc" for descending. Used to customize sort direction for the list.

file_url.description:
Updated storage location URI for the attachment file, if the file is being replaced.

Should be a valid URI string, pointing to the newly uploaded file or image when updating the attachment.

original_filename.description:
Updated filename as originally uploaded by the user.

If the name is being changed (e.g., corrected for spelling, case, or extension), must meet length and naming validation. Duplicate filenames within the same comment are not permitted (see database unique constraint on (discussion_board_comment_id, original_filename)).

mime_type.description:
Updated MIME type of the attachment (e.g., 'image/png', 'application/pdf').

Should be set if the file is replaced or changed. Only valid MIME types are accepted. Used for file validation, display, and content negotiation.

file_size_bytes.description:
Updated file size in bytes. If supplied, must be 1 (not zero) through 10,485,760 bytes (10 MB, inclusive).

Zero-sized or negative-size updates are never permitted. Supersedes the previous value when a new file is uploaded.

IDiscussionBoardCommentAttachment.IUpdat.description:
Data for updating a discussion board comment's file/image attachment, including file URL, name, MIME type, and size.

All fields are required for update requests, to ensure complete audit and validation. Values must adhere to business and technical constraints including allowed file types, naming, and file size (max 10MB).

The parent comment is identified by the path, not in the request body. Duplicate filenames within the same parent comment are disallowed by database uniqueness. Directly maps to fields in the discussion_board_comment_attachments table.

id.description: Unique identifier for the moderation report. Primary key generated upon creation. References the discussion_board_reports Prisma schema id column.

target_type.description: Type of entity being reported (e.g., 'article', 'comment', 'attachment'). Indicates the context for which the content moderation report is created. Aligns with discussion_board_reports.target_type.

target_id.description: Universal unique ID of the reported entity (article, comment, or attachment as determined by target_type). Not a foreign key in the database due to polymorphism, but references a corresponding principal entity. Corresponds to discussion_board_reports.target_id.

reason.description: Reason or category for submitting the report (e.g., spam, abuse, illegal content). Platform-defined categories or keywords expected. Maps to discussion_board_reports.reason.

description.description: User-supplied extended explanation or case notes for the moderation report, providing further context as necessary. Optional field, nullable by design. Corresponds to discussion_board_reports.description.

status.description: Current workflow and moderator status for the report (e.g., open, in_review, resolved, rejected, escalated). Used by moderation teams to track report lifecycle. Aligns with discussion_board_reports.status.

reporter_user_id.description: ID of the user who submitted this report, referencing the user’s account in discussion_board_users. Read-only and determined from authentication context; never accepted from client request body in create/update operations.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the moderation report was created and persisted, in ISO 8601 UTC format. Corresponds to discussion_board_reports.created_at.

updated_at.description: Timestamp of the most recent update or review to this report, in ISO 8601 UTC format. Corresponds to discussion_board_reports.updated_at.

deleted_at.description: Soft delete flag indicating report has been removed from active workflow but retained for audit/compliance. ISO 8601 datetime or null. Corresponds to discussion_board_reports.deleted_at.

IDiscussionBoardReport.description:
Moderation report entity for flagged content (articles, comments, or attachments) requiring administrative review.

Captures reports submitted by authenticated users indicating policy violations, abuse, or inappropriate content. Contains all metadata required for moderation, auditing, and compliance, including channel (target_type), reference id (target_id), reason, status, and user identity. Implements soft-delete for historical integrity.

Based on the discussion_board_reports Prisma schema. All property definitions align closely to the underlying database columns. Some properties (e.g., reporter_user_id) are read-only, never accepted from client requests, and only presented in responses.

page.description: Page index for pagination of report search results. First page is 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of items per page of report results. System-imposed upper bound for performance.

target_type.description: Optional filter by target entity type (e.g., article, comment, attachment). Case-insensitive match. Leave null for all types.

status.description: Optional filter by moderation report status (e.g., open, in_review, resolved). Case-insensitive match. Leave null for all statuses.

reason.description: Optional substring keyword filter for report reason. Partial match supported. Null to disable filter.

reporter_user_id.description: Optional filter by reporting user’s unique ID. Leave null for all reporters. Useful for admin/audit search.

created_at_from.description: Optional filter: include only reports created on or after this timestamp (ISO 8601 UTC). Null disables lower bound.

created_at_to.description: Optional filter: include only reports created on or before this timestamp (ISO 8601 UTC). Null disables upper bound.

sort_by.description: Field to sort results by. Supported: 'created_at', 'status', or null for default ordering.

sort_order.description: Sort order direction: 'asc', 'desc', or null (defaults to descending).

IDiscussionBoardReport.IRequest.description:
DTO schema for advanced filtering and pagination of moderation report search queries.

Allows administrators and moderators to search for flagged content reports using multiple optional criteria, including target type, moderation status, keyword in reason, reporter identity, and creation date range. Includes standard pagination and sort controls. All filters are optional; omitting or passing null disables individual filters.

target_type.description: Type of entity being reported (e.g., 'article', 'comment', 'attachment'). Used to distinguish the context of the moderation report.

target_id.description: ID of the reported entity (referencing articles, comments, or attachments depending on target_type). Not a foreign key due to multi-entity polymorphism, but always references business entities.

reason.description: Reason or category provided for the report (e.g., spam, abuse, illegal content).

description.description: Additional details or user explanation for the report. Optional extended text field for further clarification.

IDiscussionBoardReport.ICreate.description: DTO for creating a new moderation report. This type collects the required information—reported entity type, unique ID, reason category, and optional extended description—for abuse, spam, or violation reports raised by authenticated platform users. Reporter is derived from authentication context and not client-provided. Timestamps, status, and system-managed attributes are populated server-side.

reason.description: Updated reason or category for the moderation report (e.g., spam, abuse, illegal content, etc.). Must follow allowed platform moderation codes.

description.description: Revised or expanded user-provided details and context backing the moderation report. Field remains optional.

status.description: Administrative moderation processing status (e.g., open, in_review, resolved, rejected, escalated). Must comply with platform workflow and allowed status transitions. Not writable by users except as permitted by business rules.

IDiscussionBoardReport.IUpdate.description: Update DTO for moderation report changes. Allows partial or full update to reason, description, or status by the original reporting user or platform administrators. Only mutable/moderatable properties are present. System-managed fields such as created_at and deleted_at excluded. All fields are optional and subject to business rule and context validation.

admin_id.description: Filter by the UUID of the administrator who performed the moderation action. Only logs associated with this admin will be returned. This is a direct reference to discussion_board_admins.id.

target_type.description: Filter by the type of entity or user subjected to the moderation action (e.g., 'article', 'comment', 'user', 'attachment'). Returns logs targeting only the specified entity type. Case-sensitive. Optional - if omitted, logs for all entity types are included.

target_id.description: Filter by the UUID of the specific entity or user affected by the admin action. Only logs for the specified entity/user will be retrieved. Used in conjunction with target_type for precise filtering.

action_code.description: Filter by the moderation action's code or keyword (e.g., 'delete', 'edit', 'restore', 'suspend', 'warn'). Only logs with matching action code will be returned. Optional - if omitted, returns all action types.

note.description: Keyword for full-text search against admin notes. Returns logs whose 'note' property includes this keyword (case-insensitive substring match). Useful for deep-dive auditing and incident reviews.

created_at_from.description: Start time for filtering logs. Only events recorded at or after this ISO datetime are returned. Used for time-range auditing.

created_at_to.description: End time for filtering logs. Only events recorded at or before this ISO datetime are returned. Used for time-range auditing.

oneOf.description: Field to sort results by. Accepts 'created_at', 'admin_id', or 'action_code'. Defaults to 'created_at'.
Field to sort results by. Accepts 'created_at', 'admin_id', or 'action_code'. Defaults to 'created_at'.
Field to sort results by. Accepts 'created_at', 'admin_id', or 'action_code'. Defaults to 'created_at'.

sort_by.description: Field to sort results by. Accepts 'created_at', 'admin_id', or 'action_code'. Defaults to 'created_at'.

oneOf.description: Sort order direction. Allowed values: 'asc' for ascending, 'desc' for descending. Defaults to 'desc'.
Sort order direction. Allowed values: 'asc' for ascending, 'desc' for descending. Defaults to 'desc'.

sort_order.description: Sort order direction. Allowed values: 'asc' for ascending, 'desc' for descending. Defaults to 'desc'.

page.description: Pagination - results page number, starting from 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of logs per page. Must be between 1 and 100, inclusive. Defaults to 20.

IDiscussionBoardModerationLog.IRequest.description: Search, filter, and pagination criteria enabling administrators to retrieve moderation logs according to flexible audit parameters. Supports filtering by admin, action type, entity targeting, time range, note content, and advanced paging. All fields are optional; empty criteria yield unfiltered results. Used in PATCH /discussionBoard/admin/moderation/logs to support robust moderation review flows.

id.description: Primary Key. Uniquely identifies this moderation log entry. System-generated at insert time.

admin.description: Admin who performed this moderation action. Full context for the acting administrator, always available for join and audit purposes. References discussion_board_admins table.

target_type.description: Type of entity or user subjected to moderation action (e.g., 'article', 'comment', 'user', 'attachment'). Determines which content was moderated.

target_id.description: UUID of the entity or user affected by admin action. Used in combination with 'target_type' as a polymorphic reference. Allows precise cross-entity auditability.

action_code.description: Short, business-context code for the moderation action (e.g., 'delete', 'edit', 'suspend', 'warn'). Used for reporting, sorting, and reasoning about platform activity.

note.description: Optional human-readable explanation or note provided by the admin regarding the moderation event. Can contain incident details, business context, or links to other tickets.

created_at.description: Timestamp when this moderation action was recorded. Immutable and always present, provides the creation instant for audit timelines.

updated_at.description: Timestamp of the most recent update to the log entry. If entry was never edited, matches created_at. Used for external audit and system corrections.

deleted_at.description: Soft delete timestamp. Null if log is active. If present, log is hidden from routine lists but retained for compliance and audit purposes.

IDiscussionBoardModerationLog.description: Represents a single audit event for a moderation or administrative action on the platform. Each record is immutable and provides a full audit trail including actor (admin), target, action context, notes, and all relevant timestamps. All referenced entities must exist in normalized form at time of insertion. Essential for compliance, oversight, and incident response. Used in retrieval APIs for governance and platform transparency.

IDiscussionBoardSystemSetting.ISummary.description:
Summary of a system-level configuration setting for the discussion board platform.

Represents an individual configuration or policy entry that controls platform-wide infrastructure settings, appearance, or technical operations. Used for minimal, future-proof configuration management and to support admin auditing and rapid adaptation of platform state.

Includes human-facing descriptions and fully supports audit trail business logic (including soft deletion).

id.description: Unique identifier for the system setting entry. Primary key in the database.

key.description: Configuration key or policy identifier for this setting. Must be unique and used for programmatic retrieval and update.

value.description: Value associated with this configuration key. May encode raw value, serialized JSON, or application-specific text for flexible future business logic expansion.

description.description: Optional human-readable explanation or summary for the setting. Used for operator reference and audit trails. Nullable if not provided.

created_at.description: Timestamp of when the settings entry was first created. Used for audit trail and chronological tracking.

updated_at.description: Timestamp of the most recent update or modification to this setting. Supports change tracking and configuration drift analysis.

deleted_at.description: Timestamp indicating soft deletion or removal of this setting from business logic perspective. Nullable; only set if entry is marked as deleted.

id.description: Unique identifier for the user session. Mirrors the primary key column in the discussion_board_user_sessions table. Used to reference session records in the system.

ip.description: IP address from which the session was initiated. Matches the ip column in the database. Used for audit and access control.

href.description: Login or session establishment URL. Corresponds to the href field in the model. Used for audit and context tracking.

referrer.description: HTTP referrer at the start of the session, mapped from the referrer column. Used for tracking how login was initiated.

created_at.description: Time the session was created. Reflects the created_at timestamp in the session table.

expired_at.description: Time the session expired or ended, or null if not yet expired. Mirrors the expired_at column in the database. Nullable for active sessions.

IDiscussionBoardUserSession.ISummary.description:
Summary DTO for active or historical user session records.

Represents a traceable session for a discussion board user, including all audit- and security-relevant context fields. These summaries are included when presenting a user's logins, account activity, or when performing account management operations. For security, minimal business context is provided to avoid exposing sensitive system-level details, while still ensuring full traceability for audits and compliance.

IDiscussionBoardAdminSession.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of an admin session in the discussion board platform.

Provides key audit and context information for administrative authentication activity, including reference to associated admin, connection context, and session lifecycle. Supports security, moderation audit, and activity tracking. Sessions reference their respective admin by object, not raw ID, for contextual summary use.

Intended for use in activity history tables, moderation dashboards, and audit log reviews. Omits full details of the admin, focusing on session-level information and summary admin reference.

id.description: Primary key. Universally unique identifier for the admin session.

admin.description: Reference to the associated admin account summary. See discussion_board_admins table.

ip.description: Network IP address for this moderation session.

href.description: URL at start of session or moderation activity.

referrer.description: Referrer value for admin connection context.

created_at.description: Session creation time.

expired_at.description: Session end time, nullable until expired.

IDiscussionBoardArticle.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a discussion board article (post) created by a user or admin for economic and political debate.

This summary includes key business information for list, dashboard, and preview contexts: title, creation and update timestamps, and a reference to the author (which will always be present as either a user or admin summary as an exclusive oneOf). This makes it suitable for sort-ordering, cache updates, and display in index pages.

Each article is attributed to its creator; the 'author' object is a oneOf between a user and admin summary, exactly one always present. Both are never present, neither is ever omitted. 'updated_at' is included for freshness tracking and audit trails. The summary does not include the article 'body' for brevity and performance, as per summary DTO conventions. Field length limits for 'title' reflect business requirements from Prisma.

id.description:
Primary key. Unique article identifier as per discussion_board_articles.id in the database. Used to reference or link the article and always present for lookup operations.

UUID format guarantees global uniqueness across the platform.

title.description:
Article headline. Required. Must be between 5 and 150 characters in length, enforced at creation. Used for display in list and dashboard contexts.

Business logic ensures length limits are enforced and headline is always meaningful content.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when article was created. Used to order and audit article history.

Matches created_at column in discussion_board_articles table. Always present, never nullable.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when article was last updated. Used for cache invalidation, freshness tracking, and display to users in summary views where edit recency may matter.

Corresponds to updated_at column in discussion_board_articles and is always present, non-nullable.

oneOf.description: User author summary. Present if the article was authored by a user. Exclusive—if present, the admin author will not be.
Admin author summary. Present if the article was authored by an admin. Exclusive—never combined with user author.

author.description:
Non-null, exclusive author summary. Either a user or an admin summary will always be present—never both, never omitted.

Aligns with Prisma author_user_id and author_admin_id logic. This field is essential for attribution, audit, and display.

IDiscussionBoardArticleAttachment.ISumma.description:
Summary view schema for discussion board article attachments.

Provides all metadata needed to display a file/image attachment in lists, previews, or as an embedded reference in other schemas. Includes a reference to the parent article by summary. Enforces file size maximums (via business logic, max 10MB) and stores MIME type and original filename as audit/compliance requirements.

Reference integrity between attachment and article is always ensured via foreign keys in the database.

id.description:
Primary key. Unique attachment identifier as per discussion_board_article_attachments.id in the database table.

UUID format provides global uniqueness and audit traceability.

uri.description:
Storage URI for the file or image attachment. Always points to back-end storage (S3, GCS, etc.) and used for download or preview.

Business logic requires that all attachment blobs are stored and referenced by unique URI—not stored as base64 or direct payloads.

file_name.description:
Original filename of the uploaded attachment, as provided by the user at upload time.

This is stored for legal/audit reasons and user display interfaces.

file_type.description: MIME type of the attachment (example: image/png, application/pdf), validated at upload. Allows both client and back-end to determine safe rendering or download options.

file_size.description:
Size of attachment in bytes. Maximum 10 MB enforced by business and platform logic (10,485,760 bytes).

Used for quota enforcement and upload validation.

uploaded_at.description: Timestamp when the attachment was uploaded, as written in uploaded_at in the database. Used for audit trails and sort-ordering.

article.description: Summary of the article this attachment belongs to. Provides context for lists when attachments are queried standalone.

IDiscussionBoardComment.ISummary.description:
Summary view schema for discussion board comments.

Provides a lightweight representation of a comment on an article, used for lists, previews, and as an embedded object in other DTOs. Includes only identification and minimal context (body content, creation, and update/delete timestamps) with actor references omitted for summary performance. Omits full parent and detailed foreign key transformations unless contextually required by the view.

This summary always includes information to display basic comment content, its current lifecycle (active/edited/deleted), and timing, but does not embed actor/account context or attachments directly. For full context, use the main comment detail schema.

id.description: Primary Key for this comment.

body.description: The content text of the comment. Subject to business validation (2-1000 characters).

created_at.description: Timestamp when the comment was created.

updated_at.description: Timestamp when the comment was last edited.

oneOf.description: Soft deletion time. Set when the comment is removed for user or moderation reasons.
Null if the comment is not deleted.

deleted_at.description: Soft deletion time or null if not deleted.

IDiscussionBoardCommentAttachment.ISumma.description:
Summary information for a file or image attached to a discussion board comment.

Represents metadata required to display an attached file, such as the original filename, MIME type, file size, and storage URL, as well as reference back to its parent comment. Used in responses where full attachment detail is not required.

Does not include raw file data. Intended for summary lists or inlined reference within a comment entity. Attachment deletion always follows parent comment deletion.

id.description: Unique identifier for the attached file or image.

discussion_board_comment_id.description: ID of the parent comment that this attachment is linked to.

file_url.description: The URI where the attachment file is stored and can be accessed by authorized users.

original_filename.description: The original filename of the attachment, as uploaded by the user.

mime_type.description: MIME type of the attachment file (e.g., 'image/png', 'application/pdf').

file_size_bytes.description: File size in bytes, up to the business-rule-enforced limit of 10MB.

created_at.description: Timestamp indicating when this attachment was created/uploaded.

IDiscussionBoardReport.ISummary.description:
Summary of a user-submitted moderation report for discussion board content.

Provides a condensed record of flagged content requiring moderation review, including the reporter's profile (summary view), type and ID of the flagged object, core reason, status state, and the user-provided description if present. Designed for administrative or auditor lists—not for full report/audit detail.

Soft-deleted records are never included in summary outputs; refer to full audit/log DTOs for historical traceability. Field values may be truncated or omitted for brevity in collection use.

id.description:
Unique identifier for this moderation report entry.

References the underlying discussion_board_reports primary key UUID.

reporter.description:
Summary view of the user account that submitted this report.

Referencing IDiscussionBoardUser.ISummary enables compact display of reporter profile/context for each flagged content record, supporting efficient admin review and UI list generation.

target_type.description:
Indicates the domain entity reported (valid values: 'article', 'comment', or 'attachment').

Used by API and client logic to correctly resolve and present polymorphic flagged resource context.

target_id.description:
UUID of the flagged or reported business record. Used with target_type to resolve precise entity and UI context.

In summary view, entity context is never embedded directly—clients must resolve on demand.

reason.description:
Label or keyword stating why the content was reported, e.g., 'spam', 'abuse', 'illegal content', etc.

Used for business intelligence and moderation workflow triggers.

oneOf.description:
Additional comments or rationale provided by the reporting user.

Optional in summary output, included only if user entered. Truncated by platform for display if long.
Absent if user did not enter extra explanation for this report.

description.description:
Additional comments or rationale provided by the reporting user.

Optional in summary output, included only if user entered. Truncated by platform for display if long.

status.description:
Current process state of the report (open, in_review, resolved, etc.).

Determines visibility, next actions, and moderation queue/categorization.

created_at.description:
ISO timestamp when the report was logged by the user.

Supports time-based analytics and moderation review windows.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp of the last moderation/audit update or escalation.

Used for sorting and incident review prioritization.

IDiscussionBoardModerationLog.ISummary.description:
Summary record for a moderation or administrative action in the discussion board system.

Contains essential audit details: the acting administrator (embedded as IDiscussionBoardAdmin.ISummary), the target entity or user (by type and id), moderation action code, and timestamps. Used for moderation audit listings and analytics. Soft deletion is supported for full audit history while hiding from user logs.

id.description: Unique identifier of the moderation log entry.

admin.description: Summary of the administrator who performed the moderation or admin action. Reference to the user account from 'discussion_board_admins'.

target_type.description:
The type of entity or user subjected to this moderation action, such as 'article', 'comment', 'user', or 'attachment'.

This acts as a polymorphic indicator, allowing moderation logs to reference different entity domains without a rigid foreign-key relationship. The string content must be consistent with system entity types.

target_id.description: The unique identifier of the content or user affected by the admin action. For polymorphic summary context, resolve with (target_type, target_id) pair via reference APIs.

action_code.description: A code or keyword describing the type of action performed (e.g., 'delete', 'edit', 'restore', 'suspend', 'warn').

oneOf.description: Additional freeform explanation provided by the admin about the action taken, rationale, or relevant context.
Empty value if no notes were recorded by the acting admin for this event.

note.description: Additional freeform explanation provided by the admin about the action taken, rationale, or relevant context. Can be used for internal audit, communication, or compliance commentary.

created_at.description: Timestamp when this moderation action log entry was created.

updated_at.description: Timestamp of the most recent update to the log entry.

oneOf.description: Soft delete timestamp.
Null value if the log is currently active and visible in audit trails.

deleted_at.description: Soft delete timestamp or null if the entry is active.

access.description:
JWT access token for authenticated requests.

This token should be included in the Authorization header for subsequent
authenticated API requests as `Bearer {token}`.

refresh.description:
Refresh token for obtaining new access tokens.

This token can be used to request new access tokens when the current access
token expires, extending the user's session.

expired_at.description:
Access token expiration timestamp.

ISO 8601 date-time string indicating when the access token will expire and
can no longer be used for authentication.

refreshable_until.description:
Refresh token expiration timestamp.

ISO 8601 date-time string indicating the latest time until which the
refresh token can be used to obtain new access tokens.

IDiscussionBoardAuthorizationToken.description:
Authorization token response structure.

This interface defines the structure of the authorization token response
returned after successful user authentication. It contains both access and
refresh tokens along with their expiration information.

This token structure is automatically included in API schemas when the system
detects authorization actors in the requirements analysis phase. It provides
a standard format for JWT-based authentication across the generated backend
applications.
